newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin meets Chirac after vote win.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin meets Chirac after vote win.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin arrived for talks on Monday with conservative President Jacques Chirac who was expected to appoint him prime minister after a stunning left-wing election win.

Jospin arrived at Chirac's Elysee Palace two hours after outgoing prime minister Alain Juppe handed his resignation to Chirac after the Socialist-led opposition won a majority in Sunday's National Assembly election.
Chirac has said he will not resign even though he is entering a period of awkward power-sharing between the two ideological allies.
Jospin has promised a policy of creating jobs and cutting working hours and has said he will not impose extra austerity to ensure France qualifies for a single European currency.

Final results of Sunday's election showed the Socialists and their allies won 273 seats in the 577-seat National Assembly and the Communists 38 after Sunday's decisive runoff round. The ecologists won seven, their first seats in parliament.

The outgoing centre-right coalition, which had held 464 seats in the outgoing Assembly, crashed to 257. The far-right National Front won one and an independent on the French Caribbean island of Martinique won one seat.
